Document: Part 79 – Proceedings under the counter-terrorism act 2008, part 1 of the terrorist asset-freezing etc. act 2010 and part 1 of the sanctions and anti-money laundering act 2018

==================================================
[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.20] (6) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the specially represented party from communicating with the special advocate after the appropriate Minister has served closed material on the special advocate as mentioned in paragraph (1), but –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.20] (a) that party may only communicate with the special advocate through a legal representative in writing; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.20] (b) the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with directions given by the court, except that the special advocate may without such directions send a written acknowledgment of receipt to the specially represented party’s legal representative. ## Consideration of the appropriate Minister’s objection

## 79.21

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (1) Where the appropriate Minister objects under rule 79.20(5)(b) to a proposed communication by the special advocate or to the form in which it is proposed to be made the court will fix a hearing for the appropriate Minister and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (a) the special advocate gives notice to the court that the special advocate does not challenge the objection;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (b) the court –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (i) has previously considered an objection under rule 79.20(5)(b) to the same or substantially the same communication; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (ii) is satisfied that it would be just to uphold or dismiss that objection without a hearing; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (c) the appropriate Minister and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the issue without a hearing. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (2) If the special advocate does not challenge the objection, the special advocate must give notice of that fact to the court and to the appropriate Minister –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (a) within 14 days after the appropriate Minister serves on the special advocate a notice under rule 79.20(5)(b); or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (b) within such other period as the court may direct. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (3) Where the court fixes a hearing under paragraph (1) –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (a) the special advocate may file with the court and serve on the appropriate Minister a reply to the appropriate Minister’s objection;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (b) the appropriate Minister may file with the court and serve on the special advocate a response to the special advocate’s reply; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (c) the appropriate Minister and the special advocate must file with the court at least 7 days before the hearing a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them and which must–

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (i) give brief reasons for their contentions on each issue in dispute; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (ii) set out any proposals for the court to resolve the issues in dispute. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.21] (4) A hearing under this rule must take place in the absence of the specially represented party and that party’s legal representative. ## Modification of the general rules of evidence and disclosure

## 79.22

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (1) Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents), Part 32 (evidence) and Part 33 (miscellaneous rules about evidence) do not apply to any proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (2) Subject to the other rules in Section 2, 3 and this Section of this Part and to any directions of the court, the evidence of a witness may be given either –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (a) orally before the court; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (b) in a witness statement. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (3) The court may also receive evidence in documentary or any other form. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (4) A party is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses during any part of a hearing from which a party and that party’s legal representative are not excluded. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (4A) A special advocate is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.22] (5) The court may require a witness to give evidence on oath or by affirmation. ## Search for, filing of and service of material

## 79.23

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (1) A party (the disclosing party) must–

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (a) make a reasonable search for material relevant to the matters under consideration in the proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (b) file and serve on the other party and any special advocate material other than closed material –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (i) on which the disclosing party relies;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (ii) which adversely affects the disclosing party’s case; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (iii) omitted

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (iv) which supports the other party’s case. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (2) The factors relevant in deciding the reasonableness of a search under paragraph (1)(a) include –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (a) the amount of material involved;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (b) the nature and complexity of the proceedings;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (c) whether the material is in the control of the party making the search;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (d) the ease and expense of retrieval of any material; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (e) the significance of any material which is likely to be located during the search. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (3) The duty to search for, file and serve material under paragraph (1) continues until the proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies have been determined. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (4) Where material, other than closed material, to which the duty under paragraph (1) extends comes to a party’s attention before the proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies have been determined, that party must immediately –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (a) file it with the court;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (b) serve it on the other party; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.23] (c) serve it on any special advocate. ## Redacted material

## 79.24

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.24] Where the appropriate Minister serves on another party any evidence (including a witness statement) or material which has been redacted on grounds other than those of legal professional privilege, the appropriate Minister must –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.24] (a) notify the party that the evidence or material has been redacted and on what grounds it has been redacted;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.24] (b) file the evidence or material with the court in an unredacted form together with an explanation of the redaction. ## Application to withhold closed material

## 79.25

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (1) The appropriate Minister –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (a) must apply to the court for permission to withhold closed material from another party and that party’s legal representative in accordance with this rule; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (b) may not rely on closed material at a hearing unless a special advocate has been appointed and attends the hearing to represent the interests of that party. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (2) The appropriate Minister must file with the court and serve, at such time as the court directs, on the special advocate–

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (a) the closed material;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (b) a statement of the reasons for withholding that material from the specially represented party; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (c) if the appropriate Minister considers it possible to summarise that material without disclosing information contrary to the public interest, a summary of that material in a form which can be served on the specially represented party or that party’s legal representative. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (3) Where the appropriate Minister serves on the special advocate any closed material which has been redacted on grounds other than those of legal professional privilege –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (a) the appropriate Minister must file with the court the material in an unredacted form together with an explanation of the redactions; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (b) the court will give a direction to the appropriate Minister as to what may be redacted and what, if any, must be served on the special advocate in an unredacted form. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (4) The appropriate Minister may at any time amend or supplement material filed under this rule, but only with –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (a) the agreement of the special advocate; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.25] (b) the permission of the court. ## Consideration of the appropriate Minister’s application

## 79.26

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (1) Where the appropriate Minister applies in accordance with rule 79.25 for permission to withhold closed material the court will fix a hearing for the appropriate Minister and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (a) the special advocate gives notice to the court that the special advocate does not challenge the application;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (b) the court –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (i) has previously considered an application for permission to withhold the same or substantially the same material; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (ii) is satisfied that it would be just to give permission without a hearing; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (c) the appropriate Minister and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the issue without a hearing. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (2) If the special advocate does not challenge the application, the special advocate must give notice of that fact to the court and to the appropriate Minister –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (a) within 14 days after the appropriate Minister serves on the special advocate the material under rule 79.25(2); or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (b) within such other period as the court may direct. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (3) Where the court fixes a hearing under paragraph (1) –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (a) the special advocate may file with the court and serve on the appropriate Minister a reply to the appropriate Minister’s application;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (b) the appropriate Minister may file with the court and serve on the special advocate a response to the special advocate’s reply; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (c) the appropriate Minister and the special advocate must file with the court at least 7 days before the hearing a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them and which must–

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (i) give brief reasons for their contentions on each issue in dispute; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (ii) set out any proposals for the court to resolve the issues in dispute. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (4) A hearing under this rule must take place in the absence of the specially represented party and that party’s legal representative. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (5) The court will give permission to the appropriate Minister to withhold closed material where it considers that disclosure of that material would be contrary to the public interest. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (6) Where the court gives permission to the appropriate Minister to withhold closed material, the court will –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (a) consider whether to direct the appropriate Minister to serve a summary of that material on the specially represented party or that party’s legal representative; but

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (b) ensure that such a summary does not contain material, the disclosure of which would be contrary to the public interest. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (7) Where the court does not give permission to the appropriate Minister to withhold closed material from, or directs the appropriate Minister to serve a summary of that material on, the specially represented party or that party’s legal representative –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (a) the appropriate Minister is not required to serve that material or summary; but

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (b) if the appropriate Minister does not do so, at a hearing on notice, the court may –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (i) where it considers that the material or anything that is required to be summarised might adversely affect the appropriate Minister’s case or supports the case of the specially represented party, direct that the appropriate Minister must not rely on such material in the appropriate Minister’s case, or must make such concessions or take such other steps, as the court may specify; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.26] (ii) in any other case, direct that the appropriate Minister does not rely on the material or (as the case may be) on that which is required to be summarised. ## Failure to comply with directions

## 79.27

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.27] (1) Where a party or special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on that party or the special advocate a notice which states –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.27] (a) the respect in which that party or special advocate has failed to comply with the direction;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.27] (b) a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.27] (c) that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it, on the material available to it, if the party or special advocate fails to comply with the relevant direction within the time specified. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.27] (2) Where a party or special advocate fails to comply with such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Judgments

## 79.28

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.28] (1) When the court gives judgment in any proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies, it may withhold all or some of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give reasons without disclosing information contrary to the public interest. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.28] (2) Where the judgment of the court does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court will serve on the appropriate Minister and the special advocate a separate written judgment including those reasons. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.28] (3) Where the court serves a separate written judgment under paragraph (2), the special advocate may apply to the court to amend that judgment and the judgment under paragraph (1) on the grounds that the separate written judgment under paragraph (2) contains material not in the judgment under paragraph (1) the disclosure of which would not be contrary to the public interest. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.28] (4) The special advocate must serve a copy of the application under paragraph (3) on the appropriate Minister. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.28] (5) The court will give the special advocate and the appropriate Minister an opportunity to file written submissions and may determine the application with or without a hearing. ## Application by the appropriate Minister for reconsideration of order, direction or judgment

## 79.29

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (1) This rule applies where the court proposes, in any proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies, to serve on a party other than the appropriate Minister –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (a) notice of any order or direction made or given in the absence of the appropriate Minister; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (b) any written judgment. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (2) Before the court serves any such notice or judgment on a party other than the appropriate Minister it will first serve notice on the appropriate Minister of its intention to do so. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (3) The appropriate Minister may, within 5 days of being served with notice under paragraph (2), apply to the court to reconsider the terms of the order or direction or to review the terms of the proposed judgment if the appropriate Minister considers –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (a) the appropriate Minister’s compliance with the order or direction; or

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (b) the notification to another party of any matter contained in the judgment, order or direction,

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] would cause information to be disclosed contrary to the public interest. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (4) Where the appropriate Minister makes an application under paragraph (3), the appropriate Minister must at the same time serve on a special advocate, if one has been appointed –

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (a) a copy of the application;

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (b) a copy of the relevant document referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b); and

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (c) a copy of the notice served on the appropriate Minister pursuant to paragraph (2). [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (5) If a special advocate has been appointed, rule 79.26 (except for paragraphs (6) and (7)) will apply with any necessary modifications to the consideration of an application under paragraph (3) of this rule. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.29] (6) The court will not serve notice on a party other than the appropriate Minister as mentioned in paragraph (1) before the time for the appropriate Minister to make an application under paragraph (3) has expired. ## Supply of court documents

## 79.30

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.30] Unless the court directs otherwise, rule 5.4 (Register of Claims), rule 5.4B (Supply of documents from court records – a party) and rule 5.4C (Supply of documents from court records –a non-party) do not apply to any proceedings to which Section 2 or 3 of this Part applies or to any document relating to such proceedings. ## V NOTIFICATION ORDERS

## Applications for a notification order

## 79.31

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.31] (1) An application for a notification order under Schedule 4 to the 2008 Act must be made in accordance with Part 8. [Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 79.31] (2) Where the defendant wishes to serve a notice under paragraph 2(4) of Schedule 4 to the 2008 Act, the defendant must file and serve the notice with an acknowledgment of service not more than 14 days after service of the claim form. ## Footnotes

## 1. 2008 c.28. Return to footnote 1

## 2. 2001 c.24. Return to footnote 2

[Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in financial restrictions proceedings and sanctions proceedings, subject to – > 2. 2001 c.24. Return to footnote 2] Updated: Monday, 6 September 2021
